prompt_blocks.text: Two unit-height rectangular pulses have equal width 4. The fixed support is $x(\tau)$ nonzero on $0 \le \tau \le 4$, and $h(t - \tau)$ has moving support [t - 4, t]. Which ordered list gives first contact, peak alignment, and last contact?

questions.correct_answer: First contact occurs at $t = 0$, peak alignment at $t = 4$, and last contact at $t = 8$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The fixed support is [0, 4] and the moving support is [t - 4, t]. First contact occurs when the right edge t reaches 0, peak alignment occurs when [t - 4, t] = [0, 4], and last contact occurs when $t - 4 = 4$.

prompt_blocks.text: Two unit-height rectangular pulses have equal width 6. The fixed support is $x(\tau)$ nonzero on $-2 \le \tau \le 4$, and $h(t - \tau)$ has moving support [t - 6, t]. Which ordered list gives first contact, peak alignment, and last contact?

questions.correct_answer: First contact occurs at $t = -2$, peak alignment at $t = 4$, and last contact at $t = 10$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The fixed support is [-2, 4] and the moving support is [t - 6, t]. First contact occurs when the right edge t reaches -2, peak alignment occurs when [t - 6, t] = [-2, 4], and last contact occurs when $t - 6 = 4$.

prompt_blocks.text: For two equal-width rectangular pulses of width 5, $x(\tau)$ is fixed on $0 \le \tau \le 5$ and $h(t - \tau)$ is supported on [t - 5, t]. What is the overlap length $L(t)$ for $0 \le t \le 5$?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: On the rising interval, t - 5 is at or to the left of 0 and t is inside [0, 5]. The overlap is therefore [0, t], so its length is $t - 0 = t$.

prompt_blocks.text: For two equal-width rectangular pulses of width 6, $x(\tau)$ is fixed on $2 \le \tau \le 8$ and $h(t - \tau)$ is supported on [t - 6, t]. What is the overlap length $L(t)$ for $2 \le t \le 8$?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: On the rising interval, t - 6 is at or to the left of 2 and t is inside [2, 8]. The overlap is therefore [2, t], so its length is t - 2.

prompt_blocks.text: For two equal-width rectangular pulses of width 5, $x(\tau)$ is fixed on $0 \le \tau \le 5$ and $h(t - \tau)$ is supported on [t - 5, t]. What is the overlap length $L(t)$ for $5 \le t \le 10$?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: On the falling interval, t - 5 is inside [0, 5] and t is at or to the right of 5. The overlap is therefore [t - 5, 5], so its length is $5 - (t - 5) = 10 - t$.

prompt_blocks.text: For two equal-width rectangular pulses of width 4, $x(\tau)$ is fixed on $0 \le \tau \le 4$ and $h(t - \tau)$ is supported on [t - 4, t]. What is the overlap length $L(t)$ for $4 \le t \le 8$?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: On the falling interval, t - 4 is inside [0, 4] and t is at or to the right of 4. The overlap is therefore [t - 4, 4], so its length is $4 - (t - 4) = 8 - t$.

prompt_blocks.text: Two equal-width rectangular pulses have width 5 and heights 2 and 3. On the rising interval $0 \le t \le 5$, the overlap length is $L(t) = t. Which expression gives y(t)$ on this interval?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The integrand equals the height product wherever the pulses overlap. Since 2 x $3 = 6$ and the rising overlap length is $L(t) = t$, the convolution value is $y(t)$ = $6L(t)$ = 6t.

prompt_blocks.text: Two equal-width rectangular pulses have width 4 and heights 3 and 5. On the falling interval $4 \le t \le 8$, the overlap length is $L(t) = 8 - t. Which expression gives y(t)$ on this interval?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Height scaling multiplies the overlap length by the product of the two pulse heights. Here 3 x $5 = 15$, so on the falling interval $y(t)$ = $15L(t)$ = 15(8 - t).

prompt_blocks.text: Two equal-width rectangular pulses have width 4 and heights 2 and 1, with first contact at $t = 0$ and last contact at $t = 8$. Which piecewise expression gives $y(t)$?

choice_blocks.latex: y(t)=\begin{cases}0, & t<0 \\ t, & 0\le t\le 4 \\ 8-t, & 4\le t\le 8 \\ 0, & t>8\end{cases}

questions.correct_answer: $y(t)=0$ for $t<0$, $y(t)$=2t for $0 \le t \le 4$, $y(t)=2$(8 - t) for $4 \le t \le 8$, and $y(t)=0$ for $t>8$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The height product is 2 x $1 = 2$. With width 4, the rising branch is 2t on $0 \le t \le 4$, the falling branch is 2(8 - t) on $4 \le t \le 8$, and the output is 0 before first contact and after last contact.

prompt_blocks.text: Two equal-width rectangular pulses each have width 3 and are supported on $1 \le t \le 4$. Their heights are 2 and 5, so first contact occurs at $t = 2$, peak alignment at $t = 5$, and last contact at $t = 8$. Which piecewise expression gives $y(t)$?

choice_blocks.latex: y(t)=\begin{cases}0, & t<2 \\ t-2, & 2\le t\le 5 \\ 8-t, & 5\le t\le 8 \\ 0, & t>8\end{cases}

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The height product is 2 x $5 = 10$. The shifted breakpoints make the rising overlap length t - 2 and the falling overlap length 8 - t, so the complete output includes zero before $t = 2$ and after $t = 8$.

prompt_blocks.text: For $x(t)=1$ on $0\let\le3$ and $h(t)=4$ on $0\let\le8$, list the ordered edge-aligned breakpoints for $y(t)=x(t)*h(t)$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The fixed support is [0,3], and $h(t-\tau)$ has moving support [t-8,t]. Match the moving right edge t with 0 and 3 to get $t=0$ and $t=3$, then match the moving left edge t-8 with 0 and 3 to get $t=8$ and $t=11$.

prompt_blocks.text: For $x(t)=5$ on $0\let\le6$ and $h(t)=2$ on $0\let\le2$, list the ordered edge-aligned breakpoints for $y(t)=x(t)*h(t)$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The fixed support is [0,6], and $h(t-\tau)$ has moving support [t-2,t]. Match the moving right edge t with 0 and 6 to get $t=0$ and $t=6$, then match the moving left edge t-2 with 0 and 6 to get $t=2$ and $t=8$. In order, the breakpoints are 0, 2, 6, and 8.

prompt_blocks.text: For the rectangular pulses shown, $x(t)=2$ on $0 \le t \le 3$ and $h(t)=5$ on $0 \le t \le 8$. Compute $y(t)$ on the growing-overlap interval $0 \le t \le 3$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: On the growing interval, the shifted support overlaps the fixed support from $\tau=0$ to $\tau=t$, so the overlap length is $L(t)=t$. The amplitude product is $2*5=10$.

prompt_blocks.text: For the rectangular pulses shown, $x(t)=4$ on $1 \le t \le 4$ and $h(t)=3$ on $0 \le t \le 7$. Compute $y(t)$ on the growing-overlap interval $1 \le t \le 4$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: On this shifted growing interval, the common nonzero interval runs from $\tau=1$ to $\tau=t$, so the overlap length is $L(t)=t-1$. The amplitude product is $4*3=12$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: On the plateau, the entire shorter support is covered, so the overlap length is the shorter width, $L(t)=3$. The amplitude product is $2*5=10$.

prompt_blocks.text: For the rectangular pulses shown, $x(t)=4$ on $0 \le t \le 6$ and $h(t)=3$ on $0 \le t \le 2$. Compute $y(t)$ on the full-overlap interval $2 \le t \le 6$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Here the shifted h support is the shorter support. During full overlap, it is fully contained in $x(\tau)$, so the overlap length is $L(t)=2$. The amplitude product is $4*3=12$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: On the shrinking interval, the overlap starts at $\tau=t-8$ and ends at $\tau=3$. Its length is $3-(t-8)=11-t$, and the amplitude product is $2*5=10$.

prompt_blocks.text: For the rectangular pulses shown, $x(t)=4$ on $0 \le t \le 6$ and $h(t)=3$ on $0 \le t \le 2$. Compute $y(t)$ on the shrinking-overlap interval $6 \le t \le 8$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Here the shifted h support is exiting the fixed x support. On $6 \le t \le 8$, the overlap runs from $\tau=t-2$ to $\tau=6$, so $L(t)=6-(t-2)=8-t$. The amplitude product is $4*3=12$.

prompt_blocks.text: For the rectangular pulses shown, $x(t)=2$ on $0 \le t \le 3$ and $h(t)=5$ on $0 \le t \le 8$. Write the complete piecewise formula for $y(t)=x(t)*h(t)$.

questions.correct_answer: $y(t)=0$ for $t<0$; 10t for $0 \le t \le 3$; 30 for $3 \le t \le 8$; 10(11-t) for $8 \le t \le 11$; 0 for $t>11$

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The ordered breakpoints are 0, 3, 8, and 11. The amplitude product is $2*5=10$, so the growing and shrinking branches scale the overlap length by 10, and the plateau value is $10*3=30$.

prompt_blocks.text: For the rectangular pulses shown, $x(t)=4$ on $0 \le t \le 6$ and $h(t)=3$ on $0 \le t \le 2$. Write the complete piecewise formula for $y(t)=x(t)*h(t)$.

questions.correct_answer: $y(t)=0$ for $t<0$; 12t for $0 \le t \le 2$; 24 for $2 \le t \le 6$; 12(8-t) for $6 \le t \le 8$; 0 for $t>8$

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The ordered breakpoints are 0, 2, 6, and 8 because h is the shorter pulse. The amplitude product is $4*3=12$, so the plateau value is $12*2=24$ and the falling branch uses the final-contact time 8.

prompt_blocks.text: For unit-height rectangular pulses with $x(\tau)=1$ on 0$\le$ $\tau$$\le$ 3 and $h(\tau)=1$ on 0$\le$ $\tau$$\le$ 3, locate the time regions where (x*h)(t) is zero, rising, and falling.

questions.correct_answer: Breakpoints: $t=0$, $t=3$, and $t=6$. The output is zero for $t<0$, rising for 0$\le$ t$\le$ 3, falling for 3$\le$ t$\le$ 6, and zero for $t>6$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The fixed support is [0, 3], and the shifted support is [t - 3, t]. First contact occurs when $t=0$. Maximum overlap occurs when [t - 3, t] aligns with [0, 3], so $t=3$. Last contact occurs when $t - 3=3$, so $t=6$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The fixed support is [0, 4], and the shifted support is [t - 4, t]. First contact occurs when $t=0$. Maximum overlap occurs when [t - 4, t] aligns with [0, 4], so $t=4$. Last contact occurs when $t - 4=4$, so $t=8$.

prompt_blocks.text: The rectangular pulses below have common width 3. Write the complete piecewise formula for (x*h)(t).

questions.correct_answer: (x*h)$(t)=0$ for $t<0$; 5t for $0 \le t \le 3$; 5(6-t) for $3 < t \le 6$; 0 for $t>6$

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The contact breakpoints are $t=0$, $t=3$, and $t=6$. The height product is 1 times 5, so the rising branch is 5t and the falling branch is 5(6 - t).

prompt_blocks.text: The rectangular pulses below have common width 4. Write the complete piecewise formula for (x*h)(t).

questions.correct_answer: (x*h)$(t)=0$ for $t<0$; 6t for $0 \le t \le 4$; 6(8-t) for $4 < t \le 8$; 0 for $t>8$

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The contact breakpoints are $t=0$, $t=4$, and $t=8$. The height product is 2 times 3, so the rising branch is 6t and the falling branch is 6(8 - t).

prompt_blocks.text: For unit-height rectangular pulses $x(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 6$ and $h(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 3$, list the ordered convolution breakpoints and name each region they define.

questions.correct_answer: Breakpoints: $t = 0$, 3, 6, 9. Regions: $t < 0$ no overlap; $0 < t < 3$ growing overlap; $3 < t < 6$ full overlap; $6 < t < 9$ shrinking overlap; $t > 9$ no overlap.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The shorter width is 3 and the longer width is 6. First contact is at $t = 0$, the growing-overlap region ends after the shorter width at $t = 3$, full overlap ends after the longer width at $t = 6$, and last contact is at $t = 6 + 3 = 9$.

prompt_blocks.text: For unit-height rectangular pulses $x(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 2$ and $h(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 7$, list the ordered convolution breakpoints and name each region they define.

questions.correct_answer: Breakpoints: $t = 0$, 2, 7, 9. Regions: $t < 0$ no overlap; $0 < t < 2$ growing overlap; $2 < t < 7$ full overlap; $7 < t < 9$ shrinking overlap; $t > 9$ no overlap.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The shorter width is 2 and the longer width is 7, even though the shorter pulse is x rather than h. The breakpoints still come from first contact, the shorter width, the longer width, and the sum of widths.

prompt_blocks.text: For unit-height rectangular pulses $x(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 6$ and $h(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 3$, identify the time intervals before first contact and after last contact where $y(t) = 0$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: First contact occurs at $t = 0$. Last contact occurs after the two support widths have passed each other, so the last-contact time is $6 + 3 = 9$. Outside that contact window, the overlap length is zero.

prompt_blocks.text: For unit-height rectangular pulses $x(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 4$ and $h(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 7$, identify the time intervals before first contact and after last contact where $y(t) = 0$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The first-contact time is still $t = 0$. The last-contact time is the sum of the two pulse widths, $4 + 7 = 11$, not the shorter width or the full-overlap interval. Before first contact and after last contact, the pulses have no common support.

prompt_blocks.text: For unit-height rectangular pulses $x(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 6$ and $h(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 3$, compute $y(t)$ on the growing-overlap interval.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The growing-overlap interval runs from first contact to the shorter width, so here it is $0 < t < 3$. On that interval, the moving support has entered from the left and the overlap interval is [0, t].

prompt_blocks.text: For unit-height rectangular pulses $x(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 4$ and $h(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 7$, compute $y(t)$ on the growing-overlap interval.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The shorter support has width 4, so the growing interval ends at $t = 4$. During $0 < t < 4$, the left edge t - 7 is still left of 0 and the right edge t lies inside the fixed support, so the overlap is [0, t].

prompt_blocks.text: For unit-height rectangular pulses $x(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 6$ and $h(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 3$, compute $y(t)$ on the full-overlap plateau interval.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The shorter pulse has width 3, so the full-overlap plateau runs from the shorter width to the longer width: $3 < t < 6$. Throughout that interval, the entire shorter pulse is overlapped, so the overlap length is constant at 3.

prompt_blocks.text: For unit-height rectangular pulses $x(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 4$ and $h(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 7$, compute $y(t)$ on the full-overlap plateau interval.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Here the shorter pulse is x, with width 4. During the plateau interval $4 < t < 7$, the wider shifted support $h(t - \tau)$ covers all of $x(\tau)$, so the overlap length is the shorter width, not the longer width.

image_slots.image_description: Draw a clean tau-axis support diagram for unit-height rectangular pulses with fixed x(tau) supported on 0 <= tau <= 6 and moving h(t - tau) supported on t - 3 <= tau <= t during the shrinking-overlap interval 6 < t < 9. Show h(t - tau) exiting to the right, shade only the remaining overlap segment from tau = t - 3 to tau = 6, and label the overlap length as 9 - t. Include a small y(t) plot highlighting only the decreasing ramp on 6 < t < 9 from height 3 to 0, with last-contact breakpoint t = 9 marked. Do not show growing, plateau, or complete piecewise formulas.

Make the moving width-7 support visibly wider than the fixed width-4 support. prompt_blocks.text: For unit-height rectangular pulses $x(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 6$ and $h(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 3$, compute $y(t)$ on the shrinking-overlap interval.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The shrinking interval starts after full overlap ends at the longer width, $t = 6$, and ends at last contact, $t = 6 + 3 = 9$. On this interval, the remaining overlap length is measured back from the last-contact time.

prompt_blocks.text: For unit-height rectangular pulses $x(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 4$ and $h(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 7$, compute $y(t)$ on the shrinking-overlap interval.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The shrinking interval begins when the wider moving pulse stops fully covering the shorter fixed pulse, at $t = 7$, and ends at last contact, $t = 4 + 7 = 11$. The overlap runs from $\tau = t - 7$ to $\tau = 4$.

prompt_blocks.text: For unit-height rectangular pulses $x(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 6$ and $h(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 3$, assemble the complete piecewise formula for $y(t)$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The ordered breakpoints are 0, 3, 6, and 9. Use zero before first contact and after last contact, the growing length t on the first nonzero interval, the shorter width 3 on the plateau, and the remaining length 9 - t on the shrinking interval.

prompt_blocks.text: For unit-height rectangular pulses $x(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 4$ and $h(t) = 1$ on $0 \le t \le 7$, assemble the complete piecewise formula for $y(t)$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The ordered breakpoints are 0, 4, 7, and 11. The plateau height is the shorter width, 4, and the shrinking ramp uses the last-contact time 11, so the final nonzero branch is 11 - t.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The overlap width is right endpoint minus left endpoint, and the integrand height is the product of the pulse heights.

prompt_blocks.text: At a fixed time, the graph shows $x(\tau) = 3$ and $h(t - \tau) = 5$ over their common nonzero interval $-2 \le \tau \le 1$. Use geometric area to find $y(t)$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The negative left endpoint does not change the rule. The overlap width is 1 - (-2), and the rectangle height is the amplitude product.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The pulses first touch at $t = 0$, fully align at $t = 3$, and separate at $t = 6$. Since both heights are 1, the area equals the overlap length.

prompt_blocks.text: A unit-height rectangular pulse $x(\tau)$ is supported on $0 \le \tau \le 5$, and the shifted unit-height pulse $h(t - \tau)$ is supported on $t - 2 \le \tau \le t$. Use geometric area cases to write $y(t)$ over the nonzero time interval.

questions.correct_answer: $y(t)=t$ for $0 \le t \le 2$, $y(t)=2$ for $2 \le t \le 5$, and $y(t)=7-t$ for $5 \le t \le 7$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The shorter pulse has width 2, so the overlap grows until $t = 2$, stays constant at length 2 until $t = 5$, and then shrinks until $t = 7$.

prompt_blocks.text: A unit-height rectangular pulse $x(\tau)$ is supported on $0 \le \tau \le 3$, and the shifted unit-height pulse $h(t - \tau)$ is supported on $t - 5 \le \tau \le t$. Use geometric area cases to write $y(t)$ over the nonzero time interval.

questions.correct_answer: $y(t)=t$ for $0 \le t \le 3$, $y(t)=3$ for $3 \le t \le 5$, and $y(t)=8-t$ for $5 \le t \le 8$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Here the fixed pulse is the shorter width, so the plateau height is 3. The overlap grows from $t = 0$ to $t = 3$, is fully overlapped from $t = 3$ to $t = 5$, and shrinks to zero by $t = 8$.

prompt_blocks.text: The overlap length for two rectangular pulses is $L(t) = t$ on $0 \le t \le 3$ and $L(t) = 6 - t$ on $3 \le t \le 6$. If the pulse heights are 4 and 1/2, use geometric area to write $y(t)$ on the nonzero intervals.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The amplitude product is 4 times 1/2, which equals 2. Multiply both overlap-length pieces by 2 and keep the same breakpoints.

prompt_blocks.text: The overlap length for two rectangular pulses is $L(t) = t$ on $0 \le t \le 2$, $L(t) = 2$ on $2 \le t \le 5$, and $L(t) = 7 - t$ on $5 \le t \le 7$. If the pulse heights are 3 and 2, use geometric area to write $y(t)$ on the nonzero intervals.

questions.correct_answer: $y(t)$=6t for $0 \le t \le 2$, $y(t)=12$ for $2 \le t \le 5$, and $y(t)=6$(7-t) for $5 \le t \le 7$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The amplitude product is 3 times 2, which equals 6. Multiply the growing, constant, and shrinking overlap-length pieces by 6 without moving any breakpoints.

prompt_blocks.text: Let $x(\tau)$ have height 3 on $0 \le \tau \le 4$, and let $h(t - \tau)$ have height 2 on $0 \le t - \tau \le 2$. Use geometric area cases to write the complete piecewise formula for $y(t)$, including where it is zero.

questions.correct_answer: $y(t)=0$ for $t<0$, $y(t)$=6t for $0 \le t \le 2$, $y(t)=12$ for $2 \le t \le 4$, $y(t)=6$(6-t) for $4 \le t \le 6$, and $y(t)=0$ for $t>6$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The shifted support is [t - 2, t], so the breakpoints are 0, 2, 4, and 6. The amplitude product is 6, which scales the growing length t, the full-overlap length 2, and the shrinking length 6 - t.

answer_explanation_blocks.latex: y(t)=\begin{cases}0, & t<0,\\ 6t, & 0\le t\le 2,\\ 12, & 2\le t\le 4,\\ 6(6-t), & 4\le t\le 6,\\ 0, & t>6.\end{cases}

prompt_blocks.text: Let $x(\tau)$ have height 1 on $1 \le \tau \le 5$, and let $h(t - \tau)$ have height 3 on $0 \le t - \tau \le 2$. Use geometric area cases to write the complete piecewise formula for $y(t)$, including where it is zero.

questions.correct_answer: $y(t)=0$ for $t<1$, $y(t)=3$(t-1) for $1 \le t \le 3$, $y(t)=6$ for $3 \le t \le 5$, $y(t)=3$(7-t) for $5 \le t \le 7$, and $y(t)=0$ for $t>7$.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The fixed support begins at $\tau = 1$, so first contact is at $t = 1$. The overlap lengths are t - 1, then 2, then 7 - t, and the amplitude product 1 times 3 scales each nonzero piece.
